references.text: Jeremiah describes God's wrath as a fire that burns forever, the same image Moses uses of God's burning anger.
Ezekiel speaks of God's wrath that will be executed, parallel to the fire that consumes in God's fury.
Amos warns of fire that consumes, like the image of God's wrath burning down to the realm of the dead.
The psalm describes smoke from God's nostrils and consuming fire from his mouth, the same poetic image of divine wrath.
Fire goes before the Lord and consumes his enemies around him, parallel to the fire that burns to the depths of the realm of the dead.
Lamentations describes how the Lord poured out his wrath like a fire that consumed Zion's foundations, a direct parallel to the mountain foundations being set ablaze.
Isaiah describes a bonfire with plenty of wood and fire; the breath of the Lord sets it alight like a stream of sulfur.
Hebrews speaks of a fearful expectation of judgment and burning zeal that will consume the adversaries.
Our God is a consuming fire, a direct reference to the image of God's wrath as fire.
Revelation describes the lake of fire as the second death, parallel to the fire that burns down to the realm of the dead.
